messages:
alex: quick sanity check before i hand this to canary — i ran the quantized Llama-3-small v1.2 build (4-bit q4_k_m) with batch_size=8 and saw ~5-7% perplexity regression on our nightly eval compared to float16. before i escalate, can we confirm ownership for: shim cache behavior, canary rollout, and the perf tuning knobs?

maria: i can own the canary run. i’ll kick off smoke tests in staging in ~15m. which branch/config do you want me to use? :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — branch is remotes/origin/quant/v1.2-lls. config snippet i used:

```
model: llm/llama3-small-v1.2
quant: q4_k_m
batching:
  max_batch_size: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
cache:
  prefix_cache_enabled: true
  kv_invalidation_mode: conservative
```

use that exact config for parity. i also toggled `kv_invalidation_mode` while debugging.

sandeep: put a regression alert on this — i’m seeing increased cache-miss ratios in the runtime traces around step 2400-2600. can you paste the inference log snippet? i’ll grep for kv::invalidate.

alex: here’s the small log sample i grabbed:

```
[2026-03-17 09:12:02] INFO runtime: batch=12 tokens=134 kv::lookup miss
[2026-03-17 09:12:02] WARN runtime: kv::invalidate triggered for key=hdr-0a3f
[2026-03-17 09:12:03] INFO runtime: fallback to full-attention path
```

jessie: i actually merged a tiny fix for kv eviction last week (PR #3421) but it only landed on main; didn’t cherry-pick to the quant branch. if the eviction heuristic is too aggressive it explains the fallback to full-attention. i can cherry-pick and open a fast PR to the quant branch.

kevin: also worth trying a small batching/caching tweak while we validate — reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 1024 and enable `prefix_cache_aggressive: false`. that'll reduce KV churn during token streaming and keep tail latency steady. suggestion config: `max_batch_tokens=1024, prefix_cache_aggressive=false`.

alex: good call. maria — if canary fails we’ll revert to float16 variant and flag a rollback. otherwise jessie, please open the cherry-pick and tag me. sandeep, can you run the runtime grep and share the correlation between cache-miss spikes and perplexity delta?

maria: starting staging canary now with alex’s config + kevin’s tweak. will post quick pass/fail. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy initiated: canary-quant-3345678901 -> staging cluster us-west-2. monitors: latencies, token-cost, eval-perf.

sandeep: running the grep now — i’ll share a tiny table in here in a sec (miss_rate, avg_latency, ppl_delta). if we see miss_rate > 3% and ppl_delta > 4% that’s actionable.

jessie: opened PR 3478 -> quant/v1.2-lls (cherry-pick of kv-evict fix). putting @alex @maria as reviewers. build is green.

maria: quick update — smoke pass looks fine for 200 requests, miss_rate ~1.2%, ppl_delta ~2.1%. letting the longer 1k-request run finish.

alex: awesome. plan: maria will own the canary, jessie will land the cherry-pick if longer run flags, sandeep will validate logs and quantify correlation, kevin will keep tuning knobs ready. i’ll cut the rollout doc and add an explicit rollback criterion. thanks all. :sparkles:

maria: if anything flakes i’ll ping this thread and attach full staging trace. otherwise will merge canary -> prod-window after 1k-run.

deploy-bot: Canary run completed: 1k requests. status=PASS. metrics: miss_rate=1.4%, ppl_delta=2.0%, tail_99_latency=420ms.

alex: closing the handoff — handing ownership to maria for final prod-window rollout, jessie to follow up with the cherry-pick PR, sandeep to file a small regression alert dashboard so we can detect recurrence. thanks everyone.
